note: GK bank item (subtopic basics): primary/secondary/tertiary definitions, secondary = industrial sector, tertiary = service sector, tertiary contributes most to GDP while employment remains in primary sector. All taught verbatim from NCERT Class X jess202 (claims c02, c05, c07, c13).

Public/private sector classification is on the basis of ownership of enterprises. Taught in ownership_systems (claim c20); the same question appears in NCERT jess202's own exercises. Practice q38 mirrors it.

Service sector generates more than half of India's GDP. The concept — tertiary sector contributes the most to GDP — is taught in sector_change (claims c12, c13); the exact percentage option in the paper is the exam's own figure and is not quoted in the NCERT pages used.
The unorganised sector is characterised by small and scattered units outside government control, low and irregular wages, insecure employment. Taught in organised_unorganised (claims c18, c19).

Sector contributing most to real Gross Value Added over the last decade = services/tertiary. The sector ranking is taught in sector_change (claims c12, c13); the GVA measure itself is treated in detail in ECO-02 (national income), not in this chapter.

Difference between GDP and NDP is depreciation (consumption of fixed capital). National-income accounting aggregates (NDP, depreciation) belong to ECO-02 (মুদ্রাস্ফীতি ও জাতীয় আয়); neither fetched source for ECO-01 states the depreciation definition, so it is not asserted here. Signposted in the gdp_basics deep text.

Which is NOT a problem of the unorganized sector. The sector's problems — low/irregular pay, no overtime or paid leave, insecure employment — are taught in organised_unorganised (claims c18, c19); practice q36 is the same item type.
Which activity is included in the secondary sector from the standpoint of sources of national income (manufacturing-type activity). Taught in three_sectors (claims c04, c05).

Mixed economy = an economy where the government and the market together answer what/how/distribution questions, with public and private sectors coexisting. Taught in ownership_systems (claims c29, c30); practice q41 mirrors it.
